title: Re-certifying the Viridis OS Decision Kernels: A Lean Proof of the Harmonization Scalar-Price Welfare Core
abstract: Viridis OS runs decision kernels whose formal cores were checked by tools that can no longer be re-run. This program restates each kernel's formal core as a sealed, self-contained Lean 4 statement and re-proves it under a pinned toolchain (Lean v4.28.0, Mathlib 8f9d9cff). This revision treats the Harmonization kernel, which coordinates N local stewards toward a shared regulation target X by broadcasting a single scalar price. Agent i has quadratic dissipation (a_i/2)(x_i - b_i)^2 with a_i > 0 and best-responds to price lambda with b_i - lambda/a_i. We give a Lean proof of the sealed statement P2.Harmonization: for N > 0 agents and any target X, (1) the clearing price lambda* = (sum b - X)/(sum 1/a) makes the aggregate best response equal X exactly, and (2) the induced allocation x* has total dissipation no greater than that of any allocation y with sum y = X, so the decentralised price equilibrium attains the centralised optimum. The proof is a restructured port of the archived canon proof: clearing follows from linearity of the aggregate best response in the price, and optimality from the equimarginal identity a_i(x*_i - b_i) = -lambda* together with the pointwise supporting-line inequality for each quadratic, whose price terms cancel by feasibility. We observe that the canon proof also replays verbatim under the pinned toolchain, that part (2) does not need N > 0, and that it fails if a curvature is allowed to be zero. We set out what the theorem settles and what it leaves to field evidence and engineering: curvature and ideal values, the quadratic model, convergence of any price-adjustment dynamics, and conformance of the deployed code. Earlier results (Carbon Continuity, Restoration, Afforestation) are retained; all four kernels sealed so far now have candidate proofs.

claims.text: For every N > 0, all real vectors a, b indexed by Fin N with every a_i > 0, and every real X: (1) sum_i br(lamStar)_i = X, where br(lam)_i = b_i - lam/a_i and lamStar = (sum_i b_i - X)/(sum_i 1/a_i); and (2) for every y with sum_i y_i = X, J(xStar) <= J(y), where J(x) = sum_i (a_i/2)(x_i - b_i)^2 and xStar_i = br(lamStar)_i.

Observation from local Lean checks, not a sealed claim: part (2) of P2.Harmonization holds without the hypothesis N > 0 (for N = 0 both dissipations are the empty sum 0), whereas it fails if a curvature may be zero: with N = 2, a = (0,1), b = (0,0), X = 1, Lean's 1/0 = 0 convention gives xStar = (0,1) with J = 1/2, while the feasible y = (1,0) has J = 0.

next_steps: All four sealed P2 kernels (Carbon Continuity, Restoration, Afforestation, Harmonization) now have candidate proofs. Next: seal and prove the remaining thirteen live kernels in business-value order; first obtain their canon sources and runtime identifiers. For Harmonization, consider follow-up statements if the live kernel relies on them: uniqueness of the minimiser (strict convexity), the equimarginal identity, and the deferred canon primal-dual (tatonnement) convergence result. Obtain kernel runtime source to check code conformance. STATEMENT_PROPOSAL.md is still absent from inputs/context. Aristotle was not used; nothing pending.
